curie: Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in 1867. She moved to Paris in 1891 to study at the University of Paris. Together with her husband Pierre Curie, she discovered the elements polonium and radium in 1898. In 1903 she shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel. In 1911 she received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, becoming the first person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences. She died in 1934 from aplastic anemia, likely caused by long-term radiation exposure.
apollo11: Apollo 11 launched from Kennedy Space Center on July 16, 1969. The crew consisted of Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins. On July 20, 1969, the lunar module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility. Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon, followed by Aldrin about 19 minutes later. Collins remained in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia. The astronauts collected about 21.5 kilograms of lunar samples. The mission returned to Earth on July 24, 1969, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean.
insulin: Insulin is a hormone produced by the beta cells of the pancreas. It lowers blood glucose by helping cells absorb sugar from the bloodstream. Insulin was first isolated in 1921 by Frederick Banting and Charles Best at the University of Toronto. The first patient to receive an insulin injection was a 14-year-old boy named Leonard Thompson in 1922. People with type 1 diabetes do not produce enough insulin and require insulin therapy. Type 2 diabetes is often managed initially with diet, exercise, and oral medications such as metformin.
python: Python is a high-level programming language created by Guido van Rossum. The first version was released in 1991. Python emphasizes code readability and uses indentation to define code blocks. Python 3.0 was released in 2008 and was not backward compatible with Python 2. Support for Python 2 officially ended on January 1, 2020. The language is maintained by the Python Software Foundation, a nonprofit organization.
northwind: Northwind Robotics reported third-quarter revenue of $412 million, an increase of 18% compared with the same quarter last year. Net income was $37 million. The company's warehouse automation segment accounted for 61% of total revenue. Chief Executive Officer Dana Whitfield said demand from logistics customers remained strong. The company raised its full-year revenue guidance to $1.6 billion. Northwind Robotics employs approximately 4,200 people and is headquartered in Pittsburgh.
